events.title: OIC 1930/1978 charges the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing with the administration of the Urban Transit Authority Act

evidence.locator: OIC 1930/1978, operative paragraph; approval stamp 13 July 1978

events.interpretation_notes: Order made (approved) 13 July 1978, a week before the corporation existed. It is express statute-assignment evidence, the basis of the UTA responsibility period proposed from 20 July 1978; it is not the body's start.

events.title: Urban Transit Authority of British Columbia established: section 2 of the Urban Transit Authority Act in force

evidence.locator: OIC 1931/1978 (approved 13 July 1978), operative paragraph bringing ss. 1-5, 8-20, 22-24 and 25(1) into force on 20 July 1978; Act s. 2 (R4E-003)

events.interpretation_notes: In-force date of the establishing section, by proclamation ordered 13 July 1978. Assent was 29 June 1978 (already held as atlas:uta-act-assent-1978). Sections 6, 7, 21 and 25(2) were not commenced by this order. Supersedes the organisation-reported 1979 (atlas:uta-created-1979) as the legal start.

events.title: Directors of the Urban Transit Authority (at least eight) to be appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council from persons holding elected municipal office

evidence.locator: Urban Transit Authority Act, SBC 1978 c. 39, s. 4; in force 20 July 1978 under OIC 1931/1978

events.interpretation_notes: An appointment relation (G3), not a line of accountability: the directors' municipal office does not make the Authority answerable to municipalities or electors. Dated from the provision's commencement.

events.title: Metro Transit Operating Company established: the Metro Transit Operating Company Act in force

evidence.locator: OIC 29/1980 (approved 10 January 1980), operative paragraph; Act s. 2 and s. 17 (R4E-006)

events.interpretation_notes: In force by proclamation on 18 January 1980. The 31 July 1979 assent (atlas:mtoc-act-assent-1979) is not the start. Commencement does not date the transfer of Hydro transit employees or property, which the Act provided for separately and which remains undated here.

events.title: Directors of the Metro Transit Operating Company (at least seven) to be appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council

evidence.locator: Metro Transit Operating Company Act, SBC 1979 c. 18, s. 4; in force 18 January 1980 (OIC 29/1980)

events.interpretation_notes: An appointment relation (G3), not an accountability line.

events.title: The Urban Transit Authority becomes British Columbia Transit: Urban Transit Authority Amendment Act, 1982 in force

evidence.locator: OIC 1534/1982 (approval stamp 12 August 1982); Act SBC 1982 c. 53, ss. 1 and 3 (R4E-008); 1991 consolidation s. 2 historical note (R4E-018) gives 12 August 1982

events.interpretation_notes: The same corporation continues under a new name; it is not a new incorporation. The order itself prints no separate in-force day; 12 August 1982 rests on its approval and the official consolidation's note. Narrows atlas:uta-renamed-bctransit-1982 (year) and supplies the proclamation date atlas:uta-amendment-1982-assent says was not found. The 1983 "merger" date is not supported.

events.title: British Columbia Transit expressly made an agent of the Crown by the replacement establishing section

evidence.locator: Urban Transit Authority Amendment Act, 1982, s. 3 (replacement s. 2(1)); in force 12 August 1982 (OIC 1534/1982)

events.interpretation_notes: Crown agency is a legal status, not a ministry line. The claim is about the express clause; it does not say the Authority had no Crown status before.

events.title: Property and rights of the Metro Transit Operating Company vested in British Columbia Transit, which becomes liable for its debts and obligations

evidence.locator: OIC 1093/1985 (approved 30 May 1985) bringing the British Columbia Transit Amendment Act (No. 2), 1985 into force on 1 June 1985; new s. 2.1 of the Transit Act (R4E-012, s. 2)

events.interpretation_notes: A transfer and assumption, not a dissolution: the provision does not dissolve MTOC, and OIC 1096/1985 appointed a new MTOC board effective the same day. Assent was 24 May 1985; the order's 30 May approval is not the transfer date.

events.title: Metro Transit Operating Company employees transferred to British Columbia Transit

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1984/85 as reproduced in the Auditor General's 1986 report, note 18(e), printed B21; OIC 1094/1985 (R4E-014) selecting every MTOC employee under new s. 6.1

events.interpretation_notes: June 1 is stated by the Public Accounts and matches the commencement of the enabling section. OIC 1094 says only "the effective date of this order"; its 30 May approval is not the transfer date.

events.title: OIC 1096/1985 appoints nine directors of the Metro Transit Operating Company, with Stuart Milton Hodgson as chair, effective 1 June 1985

evidence.locator: OIC 1096/1985, operative paragraph ("effective June 1, 1985"); OIC 1095/1985 (R4E-015) appoints the parallel BC Transit board

events.interpretation_notes: Positive evidence that MTOC continued as a legal entity after its assets and employees passed to BC Transit. Its legal end is not established.

events.title: OIC 3495/1976 charges the Minister of Consumer and Corporate Affairs with the administration of the Liquor Distribution Act

evidence.locator: OIC 3495/1976, operative paragraph; approved 2 December 1976

events.interpretation_notes: Order made before the Act's 31 December 1976 commencement; the proposed responsibility period starts on commencement. The companion OIC 3491/1976 assigned the Liquor Control and Licensing Act to the same minister (not applied: that branch is not an atlas body).

events.title: Liquor Distribution Act in force: section 2 establishes the Liquor Distribution Branch by statute and existing government liquor stores continue under it

evidence.locator: OIC 3494/1976 (approved 2 December 1976), operative paragraph, in force 31 December 1976 except ss. 16(3) and 17(1); Act s. 2 (R4E-020); 1991 consolidation historical note (R4E-027)

events.interpretation_notes: Statutory establishment of the branch under this name. It does not date when the 1973 Liquor Administration Branch began to be called the Liquor Distribution Branch administratively (E9, still open); the body keeps its 1973 start. Supplies the in-force date atlas:ldb-act-assent-1975 says was not found.

events.title: The budgets of the Liquor Distribution Branch and the Liquor Control and Licensing Branch are separated

evidence.locator: Hansard, 1 September 1977, answer of Hon. K.R. Mair to question 97, pp. 5210-5211

events.interpretation_notes: A financial separation stated by the responsible minister later in 1977; distinct from the 1975 assent and the 31 December 1976 commencement. Not an establishment date for either branch.

events.title: Government Liquor Act and Liquor-control Plebiscites Act repealed

evidence.locator: OIC 3493/1976 (approved 2 December 1976), operative paragraph; Liquor Distribution Act s. 27 (R4E-020)

events.interpretation_notes: Repeal of the Board's 1921 statute. It is not a dissolution order for the Liquor Control Board and does not move the body's 1973 end (functions split in 1973 per BC Archives; see atlas:lcb-replaced-gla-1973-assent).

events.title: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority Act (1962) in force by proclamation, amalgamating the Power Commission and BC Electric as BC Hydro

evidence.locator: OIC 839/1962 (approved 30 March 1962): proclamation bringing the Act into force "on the 30th day of March, 1962"; Act s. 3(1), s. 28 (R4E-030)

events.interpretation_notes: The original statutory amalgamation took effect on 30 March 1962, not 31 March (the BC Archives date the body currently carries) and not the 29 March assent. The scheme was held ultra vires on 29 July 1963 and rebuilt in 1964-65; it remains the historical start of the Hydro lineage. Corroborates atlas:hydro-enacted-1962-03-30 (BC Hydro's own timeline) with the original order.

events.title: OIC 840/1962 appoints the first directors of BC Hydro, with Gordon M. Shrum and Hugh L. Keenleyside as co-chairmen

evidence.locator: OIC 840/1962, appointment paragraphs; approved 30 March 1962

events.interpretation_notes: Order-approval date under the original 1962 scheme. Gives a documented start for the co-chairmanship that atlas:hydro-cochairs-1960s only bounds to "the 1960s"; their end dates are not supplied.

events.title: Chief Justice Lett holds the Power Development Act, 1961, its 1962 amendment and the 1962 Hydro Act ultra vires

evidence.locator: BC Hydro second annual report, year ended 31 March 1964, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 19) and financial note 1, printed p. 22 (PDF p. 24)

events.interpretation_notes: Reported by Hydro's own contemporary annual report; the judgment itself was not retrieved, and no appellate outcome is asserted (the action was settled on 27 September 1963).

events.title: Settlement agreement with British Columbia Power Corporation over the BC Electric shares; total compensation $197,114,358

evidence.locator: BC Hydro second annual report, printed p. 17 and note 1, printed p. 22; ratified by the Power Measures Act, 1964 (R4E-038)

events.interpretation_notes: Agreement date. Separate from the 1961 vesting (already held as atlas:hydro-pda-1961-vesting) and the 1965 amalgamation.

events.title: British Columbia Electric Company Limited Acquisition Act assented: acquisition of all common shares authorized as at 1 August 1961

evidence.locator: SBC 1964 c. 6, assent heading and ss. 2-3

events.interpretation_notes: Enacted 20 March 1964 with retroactive effect to 1 August 1961; the body's 1961-08-01 start is the deemed date and stays.

events.title: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority Act, 1964 in force: the Authority constituted anew as a Crown agent, with the Minister of Finance as fiscal agent and directors appointed by the Lieutenant Governor in Council

evidence.locator: OIC 2519/1964, recital 4 (the Act "came into force and effect on the Proclamation" of 23 March 1964); OIC 773/1964 (R4E-036); Act ss. 3-6, 58 (R4E-035)

events.interpretation_notes: The legal constitution of the present Authority after the 1963 judgment. Drawn as a change of legal basis, not a new body: the lineage starts in 1962. Crown agency, fiscal agency and appointment are typed relations; "Finance is fiscal agent" is not a ministry-responsibility period (the responsible-3 gap for 1962-1964 stands).

events.title: OIC 2386/1965 authorizes the amalgamation of the 1964 Authority, British Columbia Electric Company Limited and the British Columbia Power Commission

evidence.locator: OIC 2386/1965, pp. 1-2; approved 20 August 1965

events.interpretation_notes: Authorizing order; the agreement it calls for fixes the effective time (next event).

events.title: BC Electric and the BC Power Commission amalgamate with the 1964 Authority and cease their separate corporate existence (5 p.m. Vancouver time)

evidence.locator: Power Measures Act, 1966 (SBC 1966 c. 38), s. 3, s. 5 and Schedule clauses 1-2, printed pp. 241-242

events.interpretation_notes: Effective 5 p.m. local time, Friday 20 August 1965, under the agreement of that day, which continues the three as the Authority established by the 1964 Act. Section 5 deems the Crown-held BC Electric common shares surrendered and cancelled on the amalgamation. The 1966 Act (assented 1 April 1966) ratified it; its assent is not the amalgamation date. This is the proposed end of both predecessor records.

events.title: OIC 2387/1965 revokes and cancels the incorporation of British Columbia Electric Company Limited and declares it dissolved

evidence.locator: OIC 2387/1965, operative paragraph; approved 23 August 1965

events.interpretation_notes: A formal Companies Act cancellation after the fact: the order recites that the company had already ceased separate existence on amalgamation (20 August). It does not move the end.

events.title: The Housing Fund holds all three issued common shares of Pemco Holdings Ltd. (cost $633,511)

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed B10, Housing Fund investment schedule (columns for 31 March 1975 and 31 March 1976)

events.interpretation_notes: An observation at two balance-sheet dates (31 March 1975 and 31 March 1976), not the 1973 purchase day or instrument, and not a ministry period: a fund's holding is ownership, not accountability.

events.title: Special resolution to change the name of Pemco Holdings Ltd. to British Columbia Housing Corporation

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed F154, note 5 (subsequent event)

events.interpretation_notes: Resolution date. The name took effect with the Registrar's certificate of 7 May 1976, which the body's names already use; the resolution does not replace it.

events.title: British Columbia Steamship Company (1975) Ltd. incorporated under the Canada Corporations Act to operate the Princess Marguerite

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed F84, note 1(a); audited statements from printed F80

events.interpretation_notes: Incorporation date as stated in the company's first audited statements; the federal certificate was not obtained.

events.title: The company acquires British Columbia Steamship Company Inc., a Washington corporation used for liquor sales aboard the vessel in that state

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed F84, note 1(a)

events.interpretation_notes: Two companies: the Washington subsidiary is a separate legal entity and is not drawn.

events.title: The company's five issued shares are held by its five directors in right of the Province

evidence.locator: Public Accounts 1975/76, printed F81 (balance sheet) and F84 note 1(a)

events.interpretation_notes: Beneficial provincial ownership observed at the statement date. It is not personal ownership by the directors, and it does not name a responsible ministry (the E1 gap for this company stands).

events.title: BC Rail's $15.5 million purchase of Vancouver Wharves is raised in the Legislature as already made

evidence.locator: Hansard, 30 March 1993 (afternoon), Oral Questions, "B.C. Rail Purchase of Vancouver Wharves Ltd." (D. Symons; Hon. A. Charbonneau)

events.interpretation_notes: A latest date: the purchase was complete on or before 30 March 1993. Not the closing day (a 25 March 1993 secondary date is held, not applied). The Hansard says "B.C. Rail"; whether the buyer was the Company or its operating subsidiary BC Rail Ltd. is not stated. Vancouver Wharves is not an atlas body.

events.title: Ministerial Order 5/2004 approves the BC Rail reorganization, including transfer of BC Rail Ltd.'s 75% interest in Vancouver Wharves Limited Partnership to the Company or an affiliate

evidence.locator: Ministerial Order 5/2004, Railway Certificate 6497, signed 30 December 2003; Schedule A(j) and Schedule B

events.interpretation_notes: An approval of described transactions, not proof of closing. The interest is in a limited partnership, not shares of a company. The order's 2004 number does not change its 2003 signature date.

events.title: Harbour Board Repeal Act assented; its repeal and dissolution sections await commencement by regulation

evidence.locator: Harbour Board Repeal Act, SBC 1983 c. 5, assent heading, ss. 2, 3 and 8

events.interpretation_notes: Assent is not the dissolution: ss. 2-3 needed an order (next event). Sections 4-5 provide for transfers of assets and liabilities to BC Development Corporation and BC Railway Company on dates Cabinet fixes; those orders are not in this package.

events.title: British Columbia Harbours Board dissolved and its members' appointments terminated on repeal of the Harbour Board Act

evidence.locator: OIC 1061/1985 (approved 30 May 1985) bringing ss. 2 and 3 of the Harbour Board Repeal Act into force "by this regulation"; confirmed 30 May 1985 by Public Accounts 1984/85, printed C24, note 19(b) (R4E-017)

events.interpretation_notes: Dissolution in force. It is not the date of the asset transfers under ss. 4-5, which remain undated.

event_corrections.why: Organisation-reported year (bctransit.com). The legal establishment is now atlas:round4-uta-established-1978-07-20; keep the 1979 claim as the weaker retrospective one.

old.interpretation_notes: Act comes into force on proclamation (date not in this document). CONFLICT: BC Hydro 2012 release says "enacted" 1962-03-30; local start 1962-03-31 unverified.

new.interpretation_notes: Assent. The Act came into force on 30 March 1962 by proclamation (OIC 839/1962; atlas:round4-hydro-1962-act-in-force-1962-03-30), which explains BC Hydro's "enacted" 30 March. The 1962 Act was held ultra vires in 1963.

event_corrections.why: The proclamation date is now found.

old.interpretation_notes: In force on proclamation; date not found. Local established 1979-07-31 equals assent date, not a proven in-force date.
Act comes into force on proclamation; proclamation date not found. ...

new.interpretation_notes: Assent. In force 12 August 1982 (OIC 1534/1982; atlas:round4-bctransit-name-1982-08-12). Legal name "British Columbia Transit"; "BC Transit" is the short form used by the organisation.

old.interpretation_notes: CONFLICT: local establishes LDB in 1973; statute naming the branch is 1975 (in force on proclamation, date not found). ...

new.interpretation_notes: Assent. In force 31 December 1976 except ss. 16(3), 17(1) (OIC 3494/1976; atlas:round4-ldb-statute-in-force-1976-12-31). The body keeps its 1973 administrative start; the administrative renaming remains undated.

set.establishedMeaning: established by section 2 of the Urban Transit Authority Act, in force by proclamation (OIC 1931/1978, approved 13 July 1978); the Act was assented on 29 June 1978
set.endedMeaning: renamed British Columbia Transit (Urban Transit Authority Amendment Act, 1982, in force 12 August 1982): the corporation continued under the new name, so this ends the name, not the body

responsible.ministry: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
responsible.note: Express assignment of the Act. From the body's start, not the order's approval. The end is the 5 December 1978 cabinet change after which the portfolio was styled Municipal Affairs (ministers-1975-1991.json); this package does not date the renaming itself.

responsible.locator: OIC 1535/1982, para. (a): administration transferred "from the Minister of Municipal Affairs" to the Minister of Education
responsible.note: The same assignment continued under the renamed portfolio until OIC 1535/1982. The OICs recommended by this minister (126/1979, 10/1980, 480/1981, 168/1982) already cited corroborate it.

set.description: Crown corporation established on 20 July 1978 under the Urban Transit Authority Act to plan and fund municipal transit, its directors appointed by Cabinet from elected municipal office-holders; took over Victoria and Vancouver transit from BC Hydro in 1980 and was renamed British Columbia Transit on 12 August 1982.

old.description: Crown corporation created in 1979 to coordinate planning, marketing and funding of municipal transit; took over Victoria and Vancouver transit from BC Hydro in 1980 and was renamed BC Transit in 1982.

body_changes.why: 1979 is the organisation-reported year (bctransit.com); the establishing section commenced 20 July 1978 (OIC 1931/1978). The ministry period was inferred from recommending ministers; Round 4 supplies the express assignment (OIC 1930/1978) and the transfer out (OIC 1535/1982). Replace the responsible-1.json UTA row with the two rows. The 1980 operations takeover is left as held (year only; still unresolved).

set.establishedMeaning: renamed from the Urban Transit Authority, and made an agent of the Crown, by the Urban Transit Authority Amendment Act, 1982 (OIC 1534/1982): the same corporation, established on 20 July 1978

responsible_remove.why: Before the name existed; the period moves to the Urban Transit Authority (above).

set.description: Provincial transit Crown corporation: the Urban Transit Authority (1978) renamed British Columbia Transit on 12 August 1982. It took over the Metro Transit Operating Company's property, obligations and employees on 1 June 1985, handed Metro Vancouver transit to TransLink in 1999 and now coordinates transit elsewhere in the province.

old.description: Provincial transit Crown corporation, renamed from the Urban Transit Authority in 1982; it handed Metro Vancouver transit to TransLink in 1999 and now coordinates transit elsewhere in the province.

body_changes.why: E9: BC Transit starts with the 1982 rename, not a 1983 merger. MTOC was not amalgamated into it: its property, rights, obligations and employees were transferred on 1 June 1985 while MTOC kept a board, so MTOC belongs in serviceSuccessorIds, not predecessorIds. The Education (1982-08-12) and Human Resources (1983-05-26) periods from OIC 1535/1982 and 850/1983 are already held in responsible-1.json and are not repeated.

set.establishedMeaning: established by the Metro Transit Operating Company Act, in force by proclamation (OIC 29/1980, approved 10 January 1980); the Act was assented on 31 July 1979
set.endedMeaning: emptied: its property, rights, debts, obligations and employees passed to British Columbia Transit (BC Transit Amendment Act (No. 2), 1985; OIC 1093/1985). It was not dissolved then, since a new board was appointed from the same day (OIC 1096/1985) and its Act was still in the 1991 consolidation, so its legal end is unknown
set.description: Crown corporation established on 18 January 1980 under the Metro Transit Operating Company Act to operate Vancouver-area transit, with a Cabinet-appointed board. On 1 June 1985 its property, obligations and employees passed to British Columbia Transit; the company itself was not dissolved then, and when it ended in law is not known.

old.description: Crown corporation established by the Metro Transit Operating Company Act to operate Vancouver-area transit; merged with the Urban Transit Authority into BC Transit.

body_changes.why: 1979-07-31 is the assent (atlas:mtoc-act-assent-1979 already says so); 1983 came from Wikipedia. Round 4 supplies the commencement and the 1985 transfer chain. Choice for the reviewer: ending the drawn body on the transfer day (proposed) shows when it stopped operating; leaving ended null would draw an empty shell to 2026. The endedMeaning says plainly that this is not a legal end.

set.establishedMeaning: proclaimed under the 1962 British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority Act (OIC 839/1962), amalgamating the Power Commission and BC Electric. That Act was held ultra vires on 29 July 1963; the Authority was constituted anew under the 1964 Act (in force 23 March 1964), and the amalgamation took effect at 5 p.m. on 20 August 1965. BC Archives gives 31 March 1962

conflicts.why: BC Archives authority record (retrospective); the proclamation order fixes 30 March 1962

set.description: Provincial electric utility. The 1962 Act amalgamating the nationalized BC Electric Company with the BC Power Commission was struck down in 1963; the Authority was reconstituted by the 1964 Act and absorbed both on 20 August 1965. It shed its gas and transit operations from 1979 and re-absorbed BC Transmission Corporation in 2010.

old.description: Provincial electric utility formed by merging the nationalized BC Electric Company with the BC Power Commission; it shed its gas and transit operations from 1979 and re-absorbed BC Transmission Corporation in 2010.

body_changes.why: E9 (Hydro 1961 or 1962): the original order puts the 1962 commencement on 30 March; 1961 is BC Electric's vesting, already a separate record. The 1964 reconstitution and 1965 amalgamation are added as events, not as a second start.

set.endedMeaning: amalgamated with the reconstituted Authority, at 5 p.m. Vancouver time (agreement ratified by the Power Measures Act, 1966); the statutory amalgamation of 30 March 1962 had been held ultra vires in 1963. It was formally dissolved by OIC 2387/1965 on 23 August 1965
set.description: The private BC Electric utility, whose shares were vested in the Crown with effect from 2 p.m. on 1 August 1961 (confirmed retroactively in 1964 after the 1963 judgment and settlement). It operated with the Power Commission as BC Hydro from 1962 and was amalgamated into the Authority on 20 August 1965.

old.description: The private BC Electric utility, expropriated by the provincial government on 1 August 1961 and merged with the BC Power Commission in 1962 to form BC Hydro.

body_changes.why: The 1962 end rested on the invalidated scheme and was a day late even for that (30 March). The agreement in the 1966 Act fixes when separate existence ended. This draws the company beside BC Hydro from 1962 to 1965, which is the legal position; if the reviewer prefers the operational picture, keep 1962-03-30 and carry 1965-08-20 as the legal end in endedMeaning instead (not recommended: a rename or invalid merger is not an ending).

set.endedMeaning: amalgamated with the reconstituted Authority, at 5 p.m. Vancouver time (Power Measures Act, 1966, Schedule clauses 1-2); the statutory amalgamation of 30 March 1962 had been held ultra vires in 1963, and the Power Measures Act, 1964 validated its carrying on business under the Hydro name
set.description: Public utility created by the Hart government to electrify areas not served by BC Electric. Purportedly amalgamated with BC Electric as BC Hydro on 30 March 1962; after that Act was struck down it was amalgamated into the reconstituted Authority on 20 August 1965.

old.description: Public utility created by the Hart government to electrify areas not served by BC Electric; amalgamated with the nationalized BC Electric Company on 31 March 1962 to form BC Hydro.

body_changes.why: As for BC Electric. Its responsible period (Premier, 1950 to 1962-03-31, responsible-1.json) ends on the old date; leave it, since no source places the Commission 1962-1965.

set.establishedMeaning: formed when the Liquor Control Board's store functions passed to the Liquor Administration Branch (BC Archives). The Liquor Distribution Branch was established by statute on 31 December 1976, when section 2 of the Liquor Distribution Act came into force (OIC 3494/1976); when the administrative name changed is not known

responsible.ministry: Ministry of Consumer and Corporate Affairs
